posts.author: Pauline Sedge
posts.body:
I have been trying to write this since about six o'clock and I am going to stop trying to write it well.

The 17:52 ran with four coaches and they were full, which is more people than that train has carried in one go since I have been counting, which is eleven years. A lot of people who have never been on it. The driver sounded the horn at every crossing from Verity Halt to Marchfield and at Cutler's Lane somebody had put a bedsheet on the fence with THANK YOU on it in what looked like fence paint.

At Marchfield they let us stand on the platform for about twenty minutes and nobody moved us on. Then the set went away empty to the depot and that was that.

I have photographs but I am not posting them tonight.

[img:photo:marchfield-last-1752]

posts.author: A. Wrenfield
posts.body:
Thank you for writing it, Pauline.

For the record because someone will want it in five years: the final public working was 2B47, the 17:52 Verity Central to Marchfield, 4 March 2006, formed 4 vehicles (set VR-112, one vehicle swapped in that morning after a door fault on the booked set). Arrived Marchfield 18:34, two minutes early. The empty stock left at 18:56.

The last down working the previous day was cancelled at Cutler's Lane for a trespass incident, so a number of the "last train" photographs circulating are in fact from the Friday.

[quote=dmc_marchfield]table 4 the 0618 does stop at hallow, i got it on the 16th and it stopped[/quote]

The 16th was a Tuesday in the engineering period. The 06:18 was diverted and ran via Hallow with a conditional stop under the possession notice. That is not a booked call and it will not happen again until the next possession.

This is precisely the kind of thing that ends up in the errors list incorrectly and then somebody misses a train because of it, which is why I ask for table numbers and dates.

topics.title: PLEASE READ: posting photographs (size, credit, and where you stand)
topics.author: Pauline Sedge

posts.author: Pauline Sedge
posts.body:
Four things, and then I will stop.

[b]Size.[/b] 800 wide maximum. Half the people here are on dial-up and a 2 megabyte photograph is not a gift to them, it is a tax.

[b]Credit.[/b] If it is not your photograph, say whose it is. If you do not know whose it is, say that. "Found on the internet" is an acceptable answer. Passing it off as yours is not, and it has happened twice this year.

[b]Scans.[/b] If you are scanning slides, scan the whole frame including the mount edge. People crop them, decide later they cropped wrong, and the original is gone.

[b]Where you stand.[/b] Not on the ballast. Not on the crossing. Not on the bridge parapet at Hallow, I know exactly who I am talking to. We had a driver make a complaint in February and one more will cost us the goodwill we have with the depot, which we are going to want.

posts.author: Pauline Sedge
posts.body:
There is one of me.

I am not the webmaster, I do not own the domain, I cannot change your username, I cannot recover a password, I cannot delete a post you made in 2003 because you have fallen out with somebody, and I cannot make the county reopen the branch.

What I can do is read every post on four boards, which I do, in the evenings, after work.

In the last month I have had eleven private messages asking me to intervene in one argument in the Signal Box. I have read that argument. It is about a bus. I am not going to intervene in it. If it upsets you, and I understand that it does, the thread has a link at the top that stops it appearing on your screen.

If anyone would like to moderate the Signal Box I will hand it over this afternoon and say thank you every day for a year.

topics.title: What happens to the trackbed now?
topics.author: Hettie L.

posts.author: Hettie L.
posts.body:
There is a notice up at Marchfield about a footpath and cycle route feasibility study. Has anyone actually read it? It is a photocopy in a plastic wallet and the wallet has gone cloudy.

I am in two minds. A path is better than brambles and fly-tipping. But once it is a path it is never a railway again, and the rails are still down.

posts.author: Gerald Brue
posts.body:
It is never a railway again either way. I have watched this happen to two other lines and the sequence is always the same: mothball, study, path, bridge deck removed for safety, done.

The bridge at Hallow is the one to watch. The moment that deck comes out the corridor is severed and everything after that is sentiment.

I would still rather have the path than the brambles. I want to be clear that I am not arguing against it. I am saying let us not pretend it is reversible.
